correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the proof over an arbitrary field. Writing x=(u,a), y=(v,b), z=(w,c), the fixed product has V-component bu and zero scalar component. LD4 forces the second product into V since d≥1, and LD2 with z=t forces the pure V×V and Kt×Kt products to vanish by subtraction, not division. Put the surviving second product equal to bPu−aEv. LD5 compares bcPu with bcP²u−acPEv. In LD3 the left is bcP²u−acPEv and the right is bcPu−acEPv+ab(E²−E)w. Independent scalar and vector choices give precisely the four displayed operator relations, and these comparisons also establish sufficiency; LD1, LD2 and LD4 then follow from the formula. Every automorphism preserves the square span V. The two equations v⊣t=v and t⊣t=0 force t to be fixed. Simultaneous conjugacy is thus the orbit problem on ordered decompositions, with block-diagonal stabilizer. For the growth and tail statements, the GL Euler products are bounded uniformly above and below for fixed q. The exponent is 2d²/3 minus the squared centered norm; a balanced triple loses at most 2/3 from 2d²/3, and the Gaussian lattice sum is uniformly bounded (only three shifts occur). Pulling out q^(−t²/2) and summing the remaining half-strength Gaussian proves the tail. CHECK_OUTPUT.txt samples small prime fields only; the all-field and fixed-q results rely on the argument, not on those tests.

value.rationale: This is a natural all-dimensional extension of a studied low-dimensional dialgebra problem, not an extra entry in the same dimension-three table. The uniform all-field classification gives an explicit complete invariant for compatible products, including in positive characteristic, and the finite-field distribution specifies how isomorphism types are weighted when a labelled product is chosen uniformly. The routine stabilizer computation is useful as part of this structural result, not a standalone contribution.
